name: CPI Retail Inflation
summary: Up from 5.54% in Sep; food inflation jumped to 8.94%, crossing RBI's 6% upper comfort limit.
plainEnglishDefinition: Measures how fast everyday household prices (groceries, rent, fuel, healthcare, and education) are rising compared to one year ago.
whyItMatters: The Reserve Bank of India aims to keep retail inflation inside a 2% to 6% comfort band (targeting 4%). Because prices usually surge only after strong demand has been running for a while, inflation acts like a rearview mirror confirming an overheating boom.
everydayIndianExample: If your monthly family kitchen and household budget in Mumbai or Bengaluru was Rs. 20,000 last October, buying the exact same basket now costs about Rs. 21,218, with vegetables and food items jumping nearly 9%.
goodOrBadVerdict: Warning Sign right now: Crossing 6.0% squeezes household budgets and puts pressure on the RBI to keep interest rates high (or hike again), which raises loan EMIs.

name: WPI Wholesale Inflation
summary: Up from 11.39% in Sep (3rd straight monthly rise); fuel and power surged +32.84%.
plainEnglishDefinition: Tracks bulk prices paid by factories, distributors, and wholesalers for raw materials, fuel, power, and manufactured goods before items reach retail shops.
whyItMatters: When factory input and energy costs jump for several months in a row, companies face squeezed profits and eventually pass those higher costs on to regular shoppers.
everydayIndianExample: When diesel, electricity, and bulk steel costs jump sharply for an appliance maker in Pune, the price tag on refrigerators and washing machines at local stores usually climbs a few months later.
goodOrBadVerdict: Warning Sign right now: Three straight months of double-digit wholesale price rises show strong cost pressures building inside the supply chain.

name: Unemployment Rate (PLFS)
summary: Down from 5.0% in Sep and 5.5% in Jun 2026, showing a strong and tightening job market.
plainEnglishDefinition: Shows the percentage of people actively looking for work who do not currently have a job.
whyItMatters: Hiring and training workers is expensive, so companies only expand headcount aggressively once they are confident business growth is real. Falling unemployment confirms a healthy expansion has been underway.
everydayIndianExample: When engineering graduates, retail staff, and delivery or logistics workers are getting hired quickly and switching jobs for better pay, the unemployment rate steadily ticks lower.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: Dropping from 5.5% in June to 4.9% in October means more Indian households are earning steady incomes, supporting everyday spending.

name: Bank Credit Growth
summary: 4th straight month above 19%; Credit-to-Deposit ratio reached 82.1% while deposits grew 16.86%.
plainEnglishDefinition: Measures how fast Indian banks are giving out new loans to families (home, car, personal loans) and businesses compared to a year ago.
whyItMatters: Healthy loan growth (around 12% to 16%) fuels business expansion. However, when lending grows much faster than bank deposits for months, banks stretch their funding and credit booms can eventually trigger overheating.
everydayIndianExample: Think of a bank branch receiving Rs. 100 in fresh fixed deposits but lending out Rs. 82+ rapidly. To attract more deposits, banks may have to offer higher FD rates and charge higher home loan rates.
goodOrBadVerdict: Watch Closely right now: Strong loan demand shows high confidence, but growing near 20% with an 82.1% Credit-to-Deposit ratio signals the credit cycle is running hot.

name: RBI Repo Rate (Policy Rate)
summary: Hiked +25 bps on Oct 7, 2026 (first hike since Feb 2023); stance shifted to 'calibrated tightening'.
plainEnglishDefinition: The benchmark interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term money to commercial banks.
whyItMatters: Central banks raise the repo rate to cool down fast-rising prices and slow excessive borrowing. Starting a rate-hike cycle is a classic late-stage boom signal.
everydayIndianExample: When the RBI raised the repo rate by 0.25% in October, floating-rate home loan borrowers immediately started seeing slightly higher EMIs or longer loan tenures, while FD savers benefit from better returns.
goodOrBadVerdict: Watch Closely right now: A 5.50% rate is still manageable, but the shift to 'calibrated tightening' means borrowing costs could climb further if inflation stays above 6%.

name: Index of Core Industries (ICI)
summary: Jumped from upwardly revised +8.2% in Sep, driven by iron ore, coal, electricity, and cement.
plainEnglishDefinition: Tracks the real-time production of India's 8 backbone industries: electricity, steel, refinery products, crude oil, coal, cement, natural gas, and fertilizers.
whyItMatters: These 8 sectors make up roughly 40% of India's industrial output. Because you cannot build highways, homes, or power factories without steel, cement, and electricity, this is a reliable live speedometer.
everydayIndianExample: Look around any growing Indian city: metro lines, expressways, apartment towers, and busy power grids directly drive surging demand for cement, steel, coal, and electricity.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: Double-digit growth (+10.9%) confirms heavy real-world construction and industrial activity is booming right now.

name: Index of Industrial Production (IIP)
summary: Strong factory output (manufacturing +7.6%, electricity +11.2%), easing slightly from +7.8% in Aug.
plainEnglishDefinition: Measures total physical production volume across Indian factories, mines, and electricity utilities compared to the same month last year.
whyItMatters: Factory production rises and falls right in sync with the broader economy, giving a much faster monthly read than quarterly GDP numbers.
everydayIndianExample: When electronics plants in Tamil Nadu, textile mills in Gujarat, and power stations nationwide run extra shifts to fill orders, IIP posts strong positive growth.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: At +6.7% with manufacturing up +7.6%, India's industrial engine is expanding at a healthy, above-average pace.

name: Conference Board CEI (India)
summary: Rebounded +3.5% month-on-month after a -2.7% dip in Aug, confirming strong current activity.
plainEnglishDefinition: A combined monthly score that blends three live Indian activity measures: industrial production, real imports, and vehicle sales.
whyItMatters: Single monthly numbers can bounce around due to weather or holidays. Blending three live indicators smooths out noise and shows the true current speed of the economy.
everydayIndianExample: Instead of judging a cricket team by one batsman's score, this index checks the combined run rate of factories, imported materials, and showroom sales together.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: A sharp +3.5% monthly rebound to 192.8 confirms August's dip was temporary and current business activity remains strong.

name: GST Collections
summary: Gross GST rose +22.9% YoY (net GST +25.6%), reflecting buoyant nationwide spending and billing.
plainEnglishDefinition: The total Goods and Services Tax collected across India each month whenever businesses sell products or services.
whyItMatters: Because GST is billed on almost every formal sale from restaurant meals to factory shipments, it acts as a live nationwide cash-register reading of consumer and business spending.
everydayIndianExample: Every time families shop during the festive season, dine out, book flights, or buy electronics, the GST on those bills flows straight into this monthly tally.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: Collecting Rs. 2.31 lakh crore (+22.9% YoY) shows robust nationwide spending and gives the government strong tax revenue.

name: Passenger Vehicle Sales
summary: Record October sales (+12.4% YoY), though growth cooled slightly from Sep's +23.3%.
plainEnglishDefinition: Counts how many new cars, SUVs, and vans automakers shipped to Indian dealerships during the month.
whyItMatters: Buying a car is one of the biggest discretionary purchases a household makes. Families only commit to multi-year car loans when they feel secure about their jobs and incomes.
everydayIndianExample: Long waiting lists for SUVs and crowded car showrooms during Navratri and Diwali show that middle-class families feel confident enough to make big-ticket purchases.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: Hitting a record 5.19 lakh units in October (+12.4% YoY) confirms household demand is strong, even if the growth rate eased slightly from September.

name: Real GDP Growth (Reference)
summary: Powered by +11.9% fixed investment growth; Q2 FY27 releases Nov 30, 2026 (consensus 7.5% to 7.6%).
plainEnglishDefinition: The broadest scorecard of the entire economy, measuring the inflation-adjusted value of all goods and services produced in India over a quarter.
whyItMatters: Real GDP is the official benchmark of economic expansion. Since India's long-term normal trend sits near 6.5% to 7.0%, growing at 7.8% confirms the economy is running above normal capacity.
everydayIndianExample: If India's economy were a family business, Real GDP growth of 7.8% means the business produced 7.8% more real goods and services this year than last year, even after removing price inflation.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: Growing at 7.8% with nearly 12% investment growth puts India firmly in expansion mode. Watch the Nov 30 Q2 release to see if growth stays near 7.5%.

name: Indian Stock Markets
summary: Sensex +2.85% weekly, Nifty +2.61%, Bank Nifty hit record 64,635.20 (4-week streak).
plainEnglishDefinition: Tracks the combined share prices of India's largest listed companies across banking, IT, energy, autos, and consumer goods.
whyItMatters: Stock investors buy shares based on what they expect company profits to look like 3 to 6 months from now, making broad stock rallies an early forward-looking signal.
everydayIndianExample: When foreign funds and Indian SIP mutual fund investors keep bidding up major banks and blue-chip companies to record levels, it signals strong expectations for upcoming corporate earnings.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: A 4-week rally and record Bank Nifty confirm investor optimism remains strong, though narrower small-cap gains mean investors are getting more selective.

name: Bond Yield Spread (10Y vs Repo)
summary: 10Y G-Sec (~7.18% to 7.19%) minus 5.50% Repo stays firmly positive (no inversion), though 364-day T-bill rose to ~6.65% (10Y-1Y spread narrowed to ~55 bps).
plainEnglishDefinition: The gap between what the Indian government pays to borrow for 10 years versus short-term borrowing rates (100 bps equals 1%).
whyItMatters: Normally, long-term interest rates sit comfortably above short-term rates. When that gap shrinks to zero or flips negative (called an inversion), bond markets are warning that a slowdown is approaching.
everydayIndianExample: Just as a 10-year fixed deposit usually pays more interest than a short-term deposit, a healthy +1.68% gap between 10-year bonds and the repo rate means banks still find lending profitable.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now (with a small caveat): A +168 bps gap shows no recession warning yet, though the tighter ~55 bps gap against 1-year T-bills reflects expectations of tighter RBI policy.

name: HSBC India PMIs
summary: Services hit 4-month high (55.8), but Manufacturing eased to 54.7 (from 55.1) with softer business optimism and rising finished-goods stocks.
plainEnglishDefinition: A monthly survey asking purchasing managers at hundreds of Indian factories and service firms whether new orders, hiring, and output are growing or shrinking. Above 50 means growing; below 50 means shrinking.
whyItMatters: Managers see new customer orders weeks before factories ship goods or report earnings. Rising unsold finished goods paired with slightly softer optimism is an early yellow flag to watch near a peak.
everydayIndianExample: If an IT and hotel services firm sees booming bookings (Services 55.8), while an auto-parts factory sees slightly slower new orders and extra boxes sitting in its warehouse, overall growth is still strong but worth monitoring.
goodOrBadVerdict: Watch Closely right now: Scores well above 50 still signal solid expansion, but cooling factory optimism and rising finished-goods inventory are classic late-cycle yellow flags.

name: Conference Board LEI (India)
summary: Rose +0.6% month-on-month after +0.8% in Aug, confirming expansion momentum remains intact.
plainEnglishDefinition: A forward-looking composite score combining 8 early-moving Indian indicators: stock prices, interest rate spreads, bank credit, exports, port cargo, capital goods output, exchange rate competitiveness, and Services PMI.
whyItMatters: Checking a combined leading index stops us from getting fooled by one noisy headline. When this broad index climbs steadily, economic growth usually continues in the coming months.
everydayIndianExample: If port cargo shipments, stock markets, machinery orders, and service business activity are all rising together, it is a strong sign the next few quarters will stay busy.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: Back-to-back monthly gains (+0.8% in Aug and +0.6% in Sep) confirm India's near-term expansion trend is still intact.

name: OECD Leading Index (CLI)
summary: Above the 100 long-term trend and still edging higher from 101.39 in Sep (and 100.26 a year ago).
plainEnglishDefinition: An international forward-looking indicator built to spot economic turning points 6 to 9 months ahead. A reading of 100 represents India's long-term normal trend.
whyItMatters: When the index sits above 100 and keeps ticking higher, it signals the economy is expanding above its normal pace with no broad downturn in sight yet.
everydayIndianExample: Think of 100 as cruising at the normal highway speed limit. At 101.45 and still edging upward, India is cruising comfortably faster than its historical average.
goodOrBadVerdict: Good right now: Sitting well above 100 and still rising gently from September confirms expansion momentum has not rolled over yet.
